provenance_warning: Every live number below comes from a LOCAL TEST RUN on the engineer's machine (server on 127.0.0.1:8801, data dir C:/Users/PC/lw/data-proof, 2-minute epochs, three desktop neurons with QA device ids proofqa-device-0001..0003). It is NOT lusca.ink. Label any footage or banner that shows these numbers 'local test run'. For production numbers, read https://lusca.ink/api/proofs and /api/health after deploy and use those instead.

facts.fact: Every epoch (60 minutes by default, on the UTC clock) LUSCA commits each contributor's confirmed credits for that epoch as a leaf of a Merkle tree, and writes a header that links to the previous epoch's header by SHA-256. The result is a hash chain of credits.
facts.source: server/proofs/index.ts (resolveEpochMinutes default 60, closesAt aligned to the epoch length); shared/proofs.ts header comment

facts.fact: A leaf is 61 bytes: 0x00, then a 4-byte epoch number, a 32-byte identity, and 8 bytes each for credits (in micro-credits), jobs and FLOPs. The leaf hash is SHA-256 of those bytes. Inner nodes are SHA-256(0x01 ‖ left ‖ right), so a leaf can never pass as a node.
facts.source: shared/proofs.ts (LEAF_BYTES = 61, leafBytes, nodeBytes); test 'leaf bytes' and 'domain separation' in server/proofs/_test.ts

facts.fact: Only confirmed credits enter a leaf. Gradient credits held in escrow enter only after a full audit confirms them. Forfeited credits never enter.
facts.source: server/proofs/_test.ts test 'genesis backfills balances; epochs commit confirmed credits only (escrow waits, forfeits never count); API auth' (real coordinator), passing

facts.fact: Epoch 0 (genesis) commits the full confirmed balance of every account at the moment proofs first start, so earlier history is covered.
facts.source: server/proofs/index.ts init(); local run genesis: 4 leaves, 2,462.28 credits (GET /api/proofs, header index 0)

facts.fact: A wallet's identity is SHA-256 of its address, so anyone can recompute it. A device's identity is an HMAC under a server secret, so device ids never appear in public data.
facts.source: server/proofs/index.ts identityFor / walletIdentity; test 'identities: wallets are public sha256, devices are keyed HMACs'

facts.fact: On /earn, 'Verify my credits' re-encodes your leaf in the browser, hashes it with WebCrypto, walks the Merkle path to the root step by step, re-hashes every header from that epoch up to the current head, and shows PASS or FAIL.
facts.source: src/components/proofs/ProofOfContribution.tsx (MyProof, linkToHead); headless Chrome QA run: epoch #10 path of 2 steps (3 leaves), result PASS, 'header is the current head #10'

facts.fact: In the local test run, 'Verify the whole chain' re-hashed 11 headers and recomputed 11 Merkle roots from the public leaves.json files in the browser in about 1.05 s.
facts.source: headless Chrome 154 QA at 1440x1000, .poc-runres text '11 headers re-hashed in this browser, genesis to head, every link holds · 11 newest roots recomputed from leaves.json · 1051 ms'

facts.fact: The browser keeps the last head it verified. The next check requires the chain to still contain exactly that header, so a rewrite of earlier history fails. The desktop neuron does the same, storing its last head in ~/.lusca.
facts.source: ProofOfContribution.tsx (readSeen/writeSeen, localStorage 'lusca.proofs.seen'); scripts/neuron.ts checkHead. QA: forged anchor gave '✗ epoch #8 no longer has the hash this browser verified on 2026-10-06 09:29 UTC (abababababab…): history was rewritten'

facts.fact: A hash chain only proves 'not rewritten' to someone who kept an earlier head hash. The page has a 'copy head hash' button so a head can be posted publicly. It is not anchored on Solana yet: not connected yet.

Anyone can download every leaf of any epoch (GET /api/proofs/:index/leaves.json) and recompute the root themselves. Closed epochs never change, so the file is served with an ETag and answers repeat requests with 304.
facts.source: server/proofs/http.ts; curl against local run: ETag present, If-None-Match → 304

facts.fact: Local test run: 13 epochs closed, 13,741.36 credits committed in 23 leaves. The ledger's lifetime credits at head #12 were 13,741.36, the same number. The server re-checked all 13 epochs ('verified').
facts.label_required: local test run; numbers grow while neurons run

facts.fact: Local test run head #12 headerHash a710ff733e85e4b7f086948e4bb665cce9e577f01de333b1e142645a90b75e3b (3 leaves, 2,458.16 credits).

facts.fact: After a hard kill (taskkill /F) and restart, the server re-verified the whole chain in 5 ms. Committed credits were unchanged (6,986.58 before and after), and the public counters did not go down: audits 725 → 744, lifetime credits 7,651.66 → 7,831.98, pages 433 → 433.
facts.source: local run: /api/proofs and /api/health before and after the kill; server log line 'proof chain verified: 10 epochs, head 9 (47816dc264e057c2…) in 5 ms'

facts.fact: Local test run: 1,556 full audits passed, 0 failed.
facts.label_required: local test run (production has its own count: read lusca.ink/api/health)

facts.fact: With per-epoch tree caching, a repeat Merkle-path lookup on a 50,000-leaf epoch takes 0.019 ms instead of 121 ms (Ryzen 7950X3D).
facts.source: benchmark script /tmp/bench-proof.mts using server/proofs/index.ts orderLeaves/treeLevels/pathFromLevels vs merklePath

facts.fact: 16 proof tests pass: Merkle vectors (1–40 leaves, odd counts, single leaf), chain verification, tamper detection, escrow and forfeits, hard-kill persistence, the save race, missing-chain refusal, API auth. The full npm test suite passes.
facts.source: npx tsx server/proofs/_test.ts → '16 proof tests passed'; npm test exit 0

facts.fact: The payout preview on /earn runs the payout engine's own planPayout() code in the browser on your period credits, for a pool size you type in SOL. Payouts are off, so it is labelled a preview and nothing is sent.
The proof does not show that the server measured the work honestly in the first place. That rests on the gradient spot checks and full audits.

moments.action: Open on the 'Proof of contribution' section. Show the open block (#N, 'closes in' countdown) at the front of the chain and the linked blocks behind it (root, leaves, credits, header hash, the 6-hex link tag between blocks).
Wait for the countdown to reach zero. The open block reads 'closing…', and a new block appears at the front within about 3 seconds.
Click 'Verify the whole chain'. Blocks flip to VERIFIED one by one; the result line says how many headers were re-hashed in this browser. The first time, it also says 'head #N saved in this browser'.
moments.why: Verification happens in the viewer's browser.

moments.action: After the next epoch closes (2 min), click 'Verify the whole chain' again. The second line reads '✓ still contains head #N … that this browser verified on …: nothing before it was rewritten'.
moments.why: The anchor: the chain only grew.

moments.action: Click 'copy head hash' in the 'your anchor' row.
moments.why: Shows how a head becomes a public anchor (for the tweet, use a lusca.ink head, not this local one).

moments.action: Click a block with 3 leaves. In the header panel, show the canonical header JSON and 'sha256 in this browser' matching. Click 'Recompute root from public leaves': '3 leaves hash to treeRoot'.
moments.why: Anyone can recompute a root from public data.

moments.action: Scroll to 'Verify my credits' and click it. The leaf bytes appear, then each hash step (leaf → h1 → h2) reveals in turn, ending in a large PASS with four ✓ lines (leaf hash, path to treeRoot, header re-hashed, header links to the current head).
moments.why: The hero moment: your own credits proven step by step.

moments.action: Click an older epoch chip (e.g. the oldest one). PASS, with 'header links to the current head #N through K headers re-hashed here'.
In 'Payout preview', type a pool (e.g. 10) in 'pool to split (SOL)'. Show the share and the 'preview · payouts are off' tag.
moments.why: The same planPayout() code the payout engine uses, clearly labelled a preview.

moments.action: Terminal of the desktop neuron (device 0001, live dashboard feed, or a --plain terminal): about 20 s after start, a line like 'proof · epoch #N root … · X credits on this device · Merkle path verified here · chain extends the head #M seen …'.
moments.why: The desktop neuron checks its own proof too.

avoid: crawler / crawl / crawling (never describe LUSCA this way)
INK points (they are 'credits'; credits are not the $INK token)
on-chain proof / anchored on Solana (the chain is not anchored on Solana yet: not connected yet)
proves the work was honest (it proves what was committed and that history you anchored was not rewritten; honesty of the work rests on the audits)
anyone can check the server never rewrote history (only someone who kept an earlier head hash can)
earn SOL now / payouts live / guaranteed payouts (payouts are off on production; the preview is a preview)
any number from the local test run presented as lusca.ink / production
20k+ audits or other production figures unless read from lusca.ink/api/health at the time of posting
numbers or claims about $CRAWL or $CLAUS (describe LUSCA's mechanism only)
slogans and hype words: revolutionary, game-changing, first ever, to the moon
